summary: This note describes the 114th United States Congress, the legislative body that met in Washington, D.C. from January 3, 2015 to January 3, 2017, during the final two years of Barack Obama's presidency. The 2014 elections gave Republicans control of both houses for the first time since the 109th Congress, and it began with the largest Republican majority since the 71st Congress. The note also lists its leadership, membership counts, and session dates.
one_line: The 114th United States Congress met from 2015 to 2017 with a Republican majority in both houses during Barack Obama's final two years as president.
key_facts: The One Hundred Fourteenth United States Congress met in Washington, D.C. from January 3, 2015, to January 3, 2017.
The 114th Congress covered the final two full years of Barack Obama's presidency.
The 2014 elections gave the Republicans control of the Senate and control of both houses of Congress for the first time since the 109th Congress.
The Congress had 248 seats in the House of Representatives and 54 seats in the Senate.
The 114th Congress began with the largest Republican majority since the 71st Congress of 1929-1931.
Joe Biden (D) served as Senate President.
Orrin Hatch (R) served as Senate President pro tempore.
John Boehner (R) served as House Speaker until October 29, 2015.
Paul Ryan (R) served as House Speaker from October 29, 2015.
The Congress had 100 senators, 435 representatives, and 6 non-voting delegates.
Both the Senate and the House had Republican majorities.
The first session ran from January 6, 2015, to December 18, 2015.
The second session ran from January 4, 2016, to January 3, 2017.
The 114th Congress followed the 113th Congress and was followed by the 115th Congress.
